diagnosis: Microinvasive carcinoma of no special type (NST)
legend: CK5 immunostaining demonstrates myoepithelial cells surrounding intermediate-grade ductal carcinoma in situ on the left and normal acini of a lobule on the right, but staining is absent around microinvasive carcinoma in the central part. Note the lymphoid reaction.

diagnosis: Ductal carcinoma in situ involving sclerosing adenosis
legend: This is a frequent mimic of microinvasive carcinoma. At low magnification, the distorted but maintained lobular architecture can be appreciated. (H&E)

diagnosis: Ductal carcinoma in situ involving sclerosing adenosis
legend: This is a frequent mimic of microinvasive carcinoma. At medium magnification, the small acini involved are suggestive of microinvasive carcinoma, with the haphazardly oriented tumour cell nests.

diagnosis: Ductal carcinoma in situ involving sclerosing adenosis
legend: This is a frequent mimic of microinvasion. Immunostaining for calponin (a cytoplasmic myoepithelial marker) reveals attenuated myoepithelium around all tumour cell clusters and nests.
The central area shows an invasive lobular carcinoma < 1 mm with oedematous stromal reaction; this is surrounded by lobular neoplasia (lobular carcinoma in situ).

diagnosis: Microinvasive carcinoma associated with high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: High-grade ductal carcinoma, which is identified as microinvasive carcinoma arising from high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ by dual immunostaining for cytokeratin and p63 (shown in Fig. <<#48269>>).

diagnosis: Microinvasive carcinoma associated with high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: Microinvasive carcinoma arising from high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ, demonstrated by dual immunostaining for cytokeratin (red) and p63 (brown).

legend: A case of high-grade ductal carcinoma in situ with scant foci of microinvasion in the adjacent tissue (< 1 mm to the margin of ductal carcinoma in situ). The presence of single-cell infiltration as seen in this case (in the top left of the field) supports the diagnosis of microinvasion.

Epithelial displacement of benign ductal cells from usual ductal hyperplasia in an intraductal papilloma is located within an area of linear fibrosis with chronic inflammation. Cell clusters have variably intact myoepithelial cells and mimic microinvasive carcinoma. (H&E)

Sclerosis at the periphery of an intraductal papilloma entraps angulated nests and glands of benign ductal cells. These histologically mimic microinvasive carcinoma, but have intact myoepithelial cells. (H&E)

diagnosis: Ductal carcinoma in situ with microinvasive carcinoma
legend: Intermediate-grade solid ductal carcinoma in situ with luminal calcification and adjacent microinvasive carcinoma.
Malignant cells with high-grade nuclei and mitotic activity have breached the basement membrane and infiltrated the stroma with surrounding inflammation.
Microinvasion is confirmed by the absence of myoepithelial cells on SMA immunohistochemistry.
HER2 immunohistochemistry highlights the focus of microinvasive carcinoma.
Small nests, glands, and single atypical cells permeate around a native lobule and elicit a desmoplastic stromal response. High-grade ductal carcinoma in situ extends into the adjacent lobules.

Small nests, glands, and single atypical cells permeate around a native lobule and elicit a desmoplastic stromal response. High-grade ductal carcinoma in situ extends into the adjacent lobules. (Higher magnification of the image shown in Fig. <<#51562>>.)

Immunohistochemical stains for p63 (brown, nuclear) and SMMHC (red, cytoplasmic) highlight intact myoepithelial cells around the normal lobules. The foci of microinvasive carcinoma lack myoepithelial cell labelling.
The microinvasive carcinoma is diffusely and strongly ER-positive.

A few sparse poorly defined epithelial-appearing cells / small clusters in reactive stroma adjacent to two acini with classic lobular carcinoma in situ are suggestive of microinvasive lobular carcinoma on H&E. Further evaluation with immunohistochemical stain(s) is recommended for definitive diagnosis (see Fig.<<#51569>>).

diagnosis: Microinvasive lobular carcinoma – supportive immunohistochemical staining
legend: Immunohistochemical staining of the focus shown in Fig.<<#51568>> supports the diagnosis of microinvasive lobular carcinoma. The microinvasive cells have lobular morphology and express CK7/18 but are devoid of myoepithelium. Focal classic lobular carcinoma in situ is present in two small acini surrounded by a continuous layer of myoepithelium (positive for basal cytokeratins CK5/14 and p63). (Triple stain: brown = nuclear p63, cytoplasmic CK5/14; red = CK7/18)
